nodes.summary: For an odd cycle transversal instance $(n, es, K)$, its graph is the graph of the edge list $es$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $es$.
nodes.title: Graph of an odd cycle transversal instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem ODD CYCLE TRANSVERSAL accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an odd cycle transversal instance $(n, es, K)$ that is well formed and feasible. Well formed means that $es$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin es$; feasible means that some set of at most $K$ vertices…
nodes.title: ODD CYCLE TRANSVERSAL as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An odd cycle transversal instance $(n, es, K)$ is feasible when there is a set $S$ of at most $K$ vertices of its graph such that the subgraph induced on the vertices outside $S$ is bipartite.
nodes.title: Feasible odd cycle transversal instances

nodes.summary: An odd cycle transversal instance is a triple $(n, es, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound on the number of removed vertices).
nodes.title: Odd cycle transversal instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem ODD CYCLE TRANSVERSAL, which accepts a bitstring exactly when it decodes to a well-formed instance $(n, es, K)$ whose graph becomes bipartite after removing some set of at most $K$ vertices, belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: ODD CYCLE TRANSVERSAL is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An odd cycle transversal instance $(n, es, K)$ is well formed when the list $es$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and $(v, u)$ does not belong to $es$.
nodes.title: Well-formed odd cycle transversal instances

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
